title: Statistical gating patterns for LLM deployments
body:
Purpose and scope:
This notes-first doc sketches a compact operational pattern for using statistical gates (not just heuristics) to manage small-batch exposures of LLM-powered features. Goal: reduce false positives/negatives in automatic roll-forward/rollback decisions while keeping human-in-the-loop for high-impact changes. Focused on text-generation/chat endpoints across Hosted and Dedicated deployments.

Intended audience:
- Release engineers and product owners running experiments
- Platform SREs and Observability owners who author signal dashboards
- Solutions/SEs who design client rollout plans

High-level pattern (one-paragraph):
1) Define a safety surface: minimal set of signals that must be computed in-stream (latency, server errors, semantic-safety token flags, user-visible failure rate).
2) Define a quality surface: downstream eval metrics computed asynchronously (human eval pass rate, reranker consistency, hallucination counts by prompt families).
3) Build a gate that combines online signals with short-window statistical tests (sequential probability ratio test or approximate Bayesian bandit check) to decide whether to: continue ramp, slow ramp, pause, or rollback.

Quick checklist before any small-batch exposure (preflight):
- Ownership: experiment lead + oncall SRE + product PM assigned
- Canary cohort defined (exact criteria and sample size; include geographic tags)
- Synthetic probes created: 50–200 deterministic prompts that exercise known edge modes
- Baseline snapshot captured: token-cost/day, p50/p95 latency, error rate, top N intents hit ratio
- Monitoring baseline dashboards wired and alerted (must include p95 latency and request-level cost estimate)
- Communication plan: Slack #rollouts, escalation contacts, 60-minute watch window after each major step

Statistical gate design (practical recipe):
- Windowing: use rolling 5–15 minute windows for operational signals (latency, 5xxs) and 60–240 minute windows for quality signals (semantic drift indicators).
- Test selection: for crash/latency/error-related gates use frequentist thresholds (p95 > baseline + X ms -> throttle). For quality regression use sequential testing: treat metric as Bernoulli (pass/fail prompt) and use SPRT (alpha=0.05, beta=0.1) to decide regression.
- Multiple comparisons: group related metrics into families (safety, latency, cost). Apply per-family correction (Benjamini-Hochberg quick-sweep) rather than per-metric Bonferroni to avoid over-conservative outcomes.
- Drift signal smoothing: apply exponential-weighted moving average with alpha tuned to ~0.2 for short signals, 0.05 for quality metrics.

Action matrix examples (operational):
- Green: no test crosses thresholds, ramp +2x exposure every 30m up to target.
- Amber: latency p95 increased by 10–30% but error rate stable -> pause ramp, increase sampling to collect more signal, notify SRE.
- Red: error rate or safety flag spike (2x baseline absolute or SPRT reject H0) -> automatic rollback to previous model variant and page SRE.
- Cost-guard: per-request token cost > baseline * 1.5 for 1h -> throttle non-essential routes (background batched requests) and notify finance contact.

Sample thresholds (starter, should be tuned per-product):
- p95 latency: +150ms absolute or +25% relative -> amber
- Server error rate (5xx): >0.5% absolute increase -> red
- Safety token flags (user-facing abusive content): any single-window increase >0.1% -> red
- Semantic non-determinism (reranker rank flip rate): >10% change in top-1 frequency over 2h -> amber

Telemetry signals (minimal set to implement in logging layer):
- request_id, model_version, route, user_cohort, region, request_tokens, response_tokens, latency_ms, status_code
- safety_flags: list of categorical flags (TOXIC, PERSONAL_INFO_LEAK, HALLUCINATION_SCORE>0.7)
- semantic_checks: pass/fail against golden answers or rule-based sanitizer for known safe intents
- economic: estimated_token_cost_usd per request (derived from runtime pricing table)

Dashboard and alert guidance:
- Primary dashboard: model-version comparison (p95 latency, 5xx rate, token cost mean/median, safety flag rate) with small multiples per cohort
- Alerting: set alert on composite gate state rather than raw metric where possible to reduce pager noise. Composite alert example: gate_state == RED for any production canary -> page SRE.
- Runbook link and last-decision log must be attached to alerts (quick links to the canary ticket).

Experiment design snippets (A/B style):
- Randomized blocked assignment: block on region and platform (mobile/web) before randomizing to preserve balance. Small-batch exposures should sample at fixed rates (e.g., 0.1%, 0.5%, 2%, 10%).
- Powering the test: because many LLM quality metrics are noisy, use stratified bootstrap over prompt families to estimate confidence intervals; target minimum effect size detection of 3–5 percentage points for pass/fail metrics.

Human-in-the-loop checkpoints:
- Daily human review queue seeded with low-confidence requests and any items flagged by safety heuristics.
- Confidence thresholds: if automated classifier confidence <0.6, surface to reviewer.
- Fast feedback loop: reviewers should add tags that feed back into metric families (false-positive-safe, false-negative-safe).

Rollback protocol (short):
- Automated rollback: trigger if gate enters RED for 2 consecutive windows (configurable) -> revert traffic to prior pinned model and re-run synthetic probe suite.
- Post-rollback review: 2-hour triage meeting required with SRE, product lead, and model owner. Capture decision and corrective actions in ticket.

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Do we prefer SPRT or Bayesian sequential testing for quality metrics? Need an A/B comparison in staging using historic signals. (ask applied-ml to run sims)
- How to encode composite gate rules in a form that non-engineers can read? (possible DSL or flowchart UI?)
- Integrate token-cost signals into routing (cost-aware fallback) — product/finance workshop needed to set acceptable thresholds.

Appendix: quick SQL-ish pseudocode for a rolling check (example)
-- compute p95 latency delta over rolling 15m windows
SELECT window_start, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) AS p95_latency, model_version
FROM requests
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '2 hours'
GROUP BY window_start, model_version;

Communication template (for human ops):
Subject: [Canary] {feature} — {model_version} — {cohort} — {GREEN|AMBER|RED}
Body: short summary of state, key signals crossed, immediate action taken, next steps, meeting link, pager contact.

Notes to self / heuristics (short bullets):
- Prefer conservative gating for safety-related signals; aggressive for purely performance-optimizations.
- Use synthetic probes to validate alerting logic before flipping on for real traffic.
- Keep a small library of golden prompt families per product area for quick A/B diagnostic runs.

References and related items:
- internal: RD-2017 (linked) — deployment routing improvements
- internal: model-onboarding checklist (Confluence page linked)

End of doc — this is intentionally compact. Next steps: schedule 1-hour sync with SRE and applied-ml to pick default SPRT params and run a 2-week simulation on historical telemetry.
